subtopics.title: Reading the Dashboard: Indicator Types and Timing

questions.question: Which list contains ONLY leading indicators?
options: Building plans passed, job advertisements, new vehicle sales, factory orders
Retail sales, industrial production, real GDP
The repo rate, the prime rate, the Gini coefficient

questions.question: Unemployment is classified as a LAGGING indicator because:
options: It is measured only once a year
Firms retrench late in a downturn and rehire cautiously in a recovery, so jobs move after the cycle turns

questions.question: 'An economy can be large and shrinking, or small and booming' warns against confusing:
options: The LEVEL of GDP with its growth RATE

questions.question: Nominal GDP grew 8% while inflation was 6%. Real growth was about:
GDP grows 1% while population grows 1,5%. GDP per capita:
options: Falls — output per person shrinks even as the economy grows

questions.question: The broadest money supply aggregate, tracked by the Reserve Bank, is:
options: M3 — M1's coins, notes and demand deposits plus all shorter and longer-term deposits

questions.question: The terms of trade IMPROVE when:
options: Export prices rise relative to import prices — a national raise earned without producing more

questions.question: The EXPANDED unemployment rate differs from the strict rate by:
options: Adding discouraged work-seekers who have given up searching

questions.question: Life expectancy is called the great summary statistic of development because:
options: It compresses nutrition, healthcare, sanitation and safety into one number
It never changes within a generation

questions.question: The infant mortality rate measures:
options: Deaths before age one per thousand live births — the most sensitive poverty gauge

questions.question: The Human Development Index blends:
options: Life expectancy, education and income per person into a score between 0 and 1

questions.question: South Africa's Gini coefficient of roughly 0,63 to 0,65 indicates:
options: That most income is earned informally
Inequality among the highest ever recorded — 0 means everyone equal, 1 means one person owns everything

subtopics.title: Comparing Countries: PPP, Pitfalls and the Global Institutions

questions.question: Purchasing power parity conversion exists because:
options: Market exchange rates understate poor countries — money buys more haircuts, taxi rides and vegetables at home than its dollar value suggests
Rich countries have higher prices for everything everywhere

questions.question: Measured gaps between rich and poor countries tend to OVERSTATE true gaps because:
options: Indicators miss the informal sector, unpaid household work and subsistence farming — all proportionally larger in poorer countries
The World Bank adjusts figures upward

questions.question: The clean one-line separation of the two Bretton Woods institutions:
options: Both lend only to rich countries
The World Bank sets exchange rates; the IMF builds dams
The IMF handles short-term crisis finance and stability; the World Bank funds long-term development projects
The IMF is private; the World Bank is a charity

questions.question: IMF loans are 'both lifelines and lightning rods' because:
options: They carry conditionality — policy changes, often austerity, demanded in exchange for the rescue

questions.question: In the taxi picture, building plans passed are headlights because:
options: Nobody passes a building plan for fun — someone intends to build next year

questions.question: Jobs are the rear-view mirror because a boss:
options: Delays retrenching when times turn bad and delays hiring until sure the recovery is real — so jobs move last

questions.question: 'Rands stretch; kilometres do not' means:
options: Distance is harder to measure than money
Money figures inflate with prices, so real comparison strips inflation out first

questions.question: South Africa's life expectancy story — collapse, then a rise of more than ten years — proves that:
options: Policy shows up in social indicators within a generation, as antiretroviral treatment demonstrated

questions.question: 'Enrolment without learning is a full classroom and an empty gauge' warns that:
options: Attendance figures flatter education unless outcomes — actual learning — are measured too

questions.question: Taps, toilets and electricity are called 'development you can touch' because:
options: Household service access measures whether growth reaches daily life — and post-1994 electrification reached about nine homes in ten
They are leading indicators of GDP

questions.question: The Gini coefficient asks:
options: How much money the country earns
However much money there is, how it is SHARED — from 0, equal, to 1, one person holding everything

questions.question: 'Divide by the passengers' means:
options: Compare living standards per capita — a giant economy can still be poor per person
Divide GDP by the number of provinces

questions.question: PPP repricing can change a country's measured standing by:
options: Doubling or more, because it values income by what it actually buys at home
Making rich countries look poorer than poor ones

questions.question: The paramedic-and-builder pairing is:
options: World Bank for crises; IMF for dams
Both institutions lend only to banks
IMF for balance-of-payments crises with conditions; World Bank for patient development lending — and SA called the paramedic in the pandemic
IMF for private firms; World Bank for governments only

questions.question: Why does a fast taxi still need its passengers checked?
options: Because GDP can rise while health, education and equality stagnate — growth is not development until it reaches human lives
